claim_checks.claim: Brief, obligations and exact plan applicability
claim_checks.judgment: Both retain the pediatric loan context, ten staff, two sites, $7,500 annual budget, no sysadmin, six-month pilot, all five required loan fields, cleaning AND checking before reassignment, plain reminders, workstation privacy, staff screen-reader use, no full-chart transfer, open amendment/retention policy and first-year integration exclusion. The P1 and P6 clarifications follow explicit brief text, not a newly invented premium specification.

claim_checks.claim: Power Apps pricing, ownership and HIPAA scope
claim_checks.judgment: The announced annual-billing list rate is $20/user/month before 2027-01-01 and $22 thereafter: ten seats give $2,400/$2,640 annual license subtotals. The announcement preserves existing subscriptions through their term and applies new pricing to purchases/renewals; the final asks for exact tenant/SKU/current quote and does not promise either subtotal as total pilot cost. Power Apps appears in Microsoft’s covered service list; the BAA does not make the customer compliant. A clinic owner/maker or paid partner remains a prerequisite, appropriate for a clinic without a sysadmin. No actual entitlement or contract was verified.

claim_checks.claim: Canvas browser versus native offline, cache and setup limits
claim_checks.judgment: Browser canvas apps cannot run offline. Dataverse offline-first canvas uses native Power Apps Mobile; local SQLite is the primary read/write cache, queued writes synchronize, and cached profile data has no automatic expiry while installed. Profile setup needs Environment Maker, System Administrator or System Customizer; the Basic User alone does not supply all offline-system-table read rights. Published canvas limitations include standalone Dataverse support and no offline Power Automate flows. OS foreground/background differences and cache-loss/revocation are appropriate proposed checks. These facts support online-first pause or separately controlled paper, not a proved native offline assignment solution.

The mobile conflict documentation describes last update per column and server validation; its conflict-detection setting does not apply to canvas. Optimistic concurrency is an explicit SDK/Web API row-version mechanism (IfRowVersionMatches), not a canvas-form toggle. The final distinguishes stale offline availability from a live server reservation and tests simultaneous assignment, delayed sync and validation rejection. A platform read does not prove the custom gate; the final does not claim it does.

claim_checks.claim: Audit history versus immutable fitting snapshot
claim_checks.judgment: Dataverse audit configuration is environment/table/column dependent. Default audit retention can be Forever, but privileged deletion and per-record DeleteAuditRecordChangeHistory exist; current native audit export is not supported and retrieval can use Web API/SDK. This is not an immutable clinical snapshot guarantee. The final explicitly treats prior/new-value amendment history as a proposed application safeguard to verify, leaves amendment authority open and proposes user/admin deletion, retention, restore/export tests. No false built-in immutability claim remains.

claim_checks.claim: WCAG and actual staff accessibility applicability
claim_checks.judgment: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 prohibits color as the only visual means; SC 2.1.1 requires keyboard operation with its path-dependent-input exception; SC 4.1.2 addresses programmatic name/role/value; SC 4.1.3 covers applicable non-focus-changing status messages. It does not require announcing every change or one mandated ARIA implementation. Both finals require actual end-to-end keyboard/screen-reader work, non-color status and focus/error checks. N1 explicitly corrects blanket announcement language. Power Apps accessibility guidance and the Jan 06, 2026 AssetTiger vendor VPAT are useful leads, not proof the clinic’s tasks pass; the latter names WAVE and has mixed support reporting. No accessibility runtime or legal conformance finding is claimed.

claim_checks.claim: Clinical cleaning, fitting units and scope boundaries
claim_checks.judgment: FDA consumer guidance supports cleaning as instructed and avoiding damaging solvents/alcohol/water; it is not a clinic reprocessing protocol. Neither final invents a disinfection recipe or fitting dB/frequency conversion. Device-specific IFUs and approved clinic procedure are honestly missing external inputs. The functional-check requirement comes directly from the brief. Native fitting field types/units remain device-dependent; operational dates/IDs/events are conceptual model choices. Minimum operational linkage is not declared anonymous and is not a full-record migration.

claim_checks.claim: Conditional privacy, retention and workstation controls
claim_checks.judgment: HHS states HIPAA itself does not set medical-record retention periods; other applicable law may and safeguards persist through disposal. Minimum-necessary guidance has treatment-disclosure/request exceptions, and internal access must be assessed by role/purpose rather than applying a blanket prohibition to treatment. Cloud ePHI handling can require a BAA even when a provider lacks a decryption key, plus the clinic’s own risk analysis. Both correctly leave jurisdiction, covered-entity status, record classification and actual agreements unresolved. Individual accounts, approved views, physical sight lines, cache/export/session checks are proposed controls, not a demonstrated privacy guarantee. Neither invents a retention duration or funded appointment integration.

claim_checks.claim: Snipe-IT hosting, data model and status applicability
claim_checks.judgment: Hosted Basic/Small Business/Dedicated pricing is $399.99/$999.99/$2,499.99 annual with unlimited users/assets; public hosting maintenance/update statements do not establish clinical suitability. Unique asset tags and Pending/Undeployable versus Deployable statuses support custody/nonassignability concepts. Custom fieldsets attach through asset models and are not demonstrated per-loan family records; encrypted field limitations/basic validators do not prove a clinical transaction model. Notifications/check-in due mechanisms are product features, not a tested caregiver preference path. Device-only use remains conditional; neither arm declares ordinary asset software a proved pediatric loan system or assumes BAA silence proves no agreement exists.

claim_checks.claim: Snipe-IT API advisory → fix → release chain
claim_checks.judgment: GHSA-qffp-xpqv-gqr4 affects versions <=8.6.3 and is patched in 8.7.0. It concerns API checkout validation against soft-deleted targets; the advisory says web equivalents were not vulnerable and reports integrity/availability rather than confidentiality impact. PR #19330 introduced exists_undeleted validation and merged at 81d0197 on July 20, 2026. v8.7.0 was released August 11 (1d05a7c); advisory publication followed August 24. v8.8.0 was listed September 30 at 2c466fa, requiring PHP >=8.2 and recommending 8.4. The final correctly avoids turning this into ordinary-web patient disclosure or product-wide failure. It is a relevant maintenance/evolution chain, not installed-release verification.

claim_checks.claim: Snipe-IT maintenance issue → permission fix → release chain
claim_checks.judgment: Issue #18951 concerns a regular user’s maintenance attachment/view permission in a v8.4.1 multiple-company/location-scoped setup. PR #18964 added a separate maintenance permission and merged May 4, 2026 at bd4150a. The maintainer expressly left historical cross-company access outside that fix. v8.5.0 at 90c8689 (May 12) lists #18951/#18964. N1 preserves those configuration and historical-access boundaries and treats current v8.8.0 as time-sensitive, not approved for deployment. This satisfies O3 independently of the separate #18750 problem.

The no-linked-fix-on-the-page assertion is false: the issue’s Aug 27 maintainer comment links #19539. That PR merged Aug 22 at e2ce943bcbc2ba770fdf4136333fbf6ef8607dd3; v8.8.0’s release body lists Requestables Overhaul and the PR. Released FulfillCheckoutRequestAction::markFullyFulfilled writes state, fulfilled_at, fulfilled_by and checkout_actionlog_id; CheckoutRequest::scopeOpen/scopePending excludes terminal states. This proves available follow-up/fix evidence, not a runtime proof every reporter path is fixed. The final’s conditional current-version regression test remains sensible. The omission is minor because requestables are optional, no product is rejected or selected on this basis, and the separately correct O3 chain is retained. It is not an honestly unavailable source and is recorded as an independent disagreement with the critic.

claim_checks.claim: Lend Engine feature/price/tier and child-data/default-policy tensions
claim_checks.judgment: Plus lists $25/month ($300 annual arithmetic), 10 sites and unlimited staff, with advertised assistive lending/prompts/custom fields/maintenance; this is a demo lead, not proved clinical fit. Policy describes day-before due email and stopping email by removing the address, not a demonstrated preference field. It defines >60 days without administrator access as inactive with permanent account deletion, says EU hosting, and has an under-13 rule/toy-library exception that does not settle staff-entered child-linked clinic data. Pricing marks SSL for all displayed plans whereas policy describes Free/Standard non-SSL and Plus SSL (with a Standard custom-domain exception). Pricing places backups on Business. N1 preserves the conflicts, exact deletion trigger and age/data-location/backup/exit questions; it neither declares the product permitted nor prohibited by law and restricts evaluation to synthetic records.

claim_checks.claim: Blueprint OMS and myTurn domain discoveries
claim_checks.judgment: Blueprint advertises hearing-clinic inventory, multi-location stock, loaner/trial history, agreements and return recalls. No reviewed primary price establishes affordability, and the final appropriately requires existing licensing or a narrow affordable module without practice-management migration. myTurn advertises multi-location lending, barcode/RFID, reminders and assistive-technology use; its highlighted June 2026 update is not claimed to be the latest release. Gate, terms, accessibility and price remain marketing-level unknowns. Retaining these as conditional inquiries is useful discovery rather than evasion or unsupported suitability.

claim_checks.claim: AssetTiger paid-plan scope, offline queue and vendor accessibility report
claim_checks.judgment: Basic annual price is $220 for up to 500 assets; paid plans list unlimited users, due-date check-in/out and maintenance. The FAQ describes offline scans queued locally without establishing conflict-safe assignment. The January 2026 VPAT is vendor-authored, identifies WAVE and contains support limitations; it is not an actual staff task result. N1 accurately keeps loan-event field scope, quarantine enforcement, collision behavior and family/session privacy as demo questions and device-only use as an option. It does not equate queueing with two-site safety or vendor audit-log marketing with independent immutability proof.

claim_checks.claim: Cheqroom work orders versus actual availability, defaults and cost
claim_checks.judgment: Operations Requests are an add-on, move Draft→Open→In Progress→Closed, and explicitly do not change item availability. A separate maintenance flag can be configured unavailable; users with maintenance permissions can still reserve/check out flagged items, which is why a flag is not a proved clinical release gate. System templates include location/description, default Low priority, typed maintenance/inspection/cleaning fields; they are customizable examples, not a required clinic schema. Business starts at $275/admin/month, covers up to three locations and custom roles: one/two admin arithmetic is $3,300/$6,600 annual before add-ons/minimums/services. N1 calls for a distinct blocking flag AND proving interactions on the actual tier, rather than asserting a universal hard block. The privileged bypass is a useful source qualification, but its omission as an explicit sentence does not create a material guarantee where none was claimed.

claim_checks.claim: AppSheet license, rows, same-row conflict, offline and SMS evolution
claim_checks.judgment: Core lists $10/user/month: ten separately purchased seats are $1,200/year; some Workspace entitlements include Core and ten test users can test free. Core AppSheet databases list 2,500 rows/database, not 2,500 generic spreadsheet rows or an unlimited-history allowance. Concurrent changes to one row are last-writer-wins; sync sends queued local changes and refreshes server/app state, with initial-online/loaded-browser/cache constraints and prolonged-offline cautions. This does not prove every offline design unsafe or a normalized schema safe. The default SMS channel was discontinued after 2025-04-21; custom Twilio remains a documented route. N1 accurately limits these claims and keeps costs, ownership, cache privacy and collision tests explicit. Vendor SOC/HIPAA-support statements are not independent legal findings.

claim_checks.claim: Alternatives, support burden and outage-process logic
claim_checks.judgment: Existing supported clinic software, hosted/device-only tooling, managed low-code, a small custom app, existing split lists and controlled paper are materially different approaches, not synonyms for a tracker. N2 narrows custom/self-hosted work for the no-sysadmin pilot but allows a funded accountable partner; N1 retains custom work with support burden. The present split lists are not promoted as a proved solution. N2’s nonoverlapping site device pools/no cross-site movement/paper reconciliation and N1’s pause until current authoritative availability avoid promising simultaneous offline allocation. These are proposed operating controls; no outage process was executed.

Both provide discriminating negative/bypass, sequential-family, two-site conflict, role, workstation, actual staff accessibility, reminder, contract and capacity/support checks. N2 adds platform audit-deletion and OS/cache tests; N1 adds vendor-policy contradictions, preference-removal and optional requestable regression. All are explicitly proposals. Authored executed work is public-source review, reveal and evidence-artifact bookkeeping; no tenant/product/runtime/real-data or clinical/legal test is claimed. Frozen artifacts permit checking the wording and source facts, not independently certifying every historical author operation. Hash/JSON/zero-exit artifacts are provenance checks, not scientific proof of a safe app.

N2.reasoning: Cleaning AND a separate functional check must precede availability; incomplete/failed/damaged/uncertain devices stay nonassignable. Retains preparation, assignment and return. Device procedure is not inferred from FDA consumer advice.

N2.reasoning: Explicitly retains all five required fields and no full-chart transfer; fitting types/units are IFU-specific. A linkable random loan key is optional and not anonymous; reception visibility remains a decision.
N2.exact_clause: P2: Associate loan records with the minimum patient and caregiver details needed for contact and handoff.

N2.reasoning: Retains screen-reader labels/non-color cues and adds actual keyboard/focus/error/status/zoom tasks. Applicable WCAG checks and actual user test do not become a vendor conformance guarantee.
N2.exact_clause: P3: Provide accessible status controls, including screen-reader labels and cues that do not depend on color.

N2.reasoning: Reminders remain required; a manual due queue is an implementation option rather than dropping them. Plain minimal content, preference/language, approved roles and physical/session privacy are explicit. Automation is conditional.
N2.exact_clause: P4: Support plain-language reminders and a staff view that limits exposure of other families' records.

N2.disposition: Explicit clinical user decision; proposed safeguard
N2.reasoning: No default editor is selected. Snapshot/amendment attribution is a proposed application safeguard, not an immutable Dataverse property or a decided legal requirement; implementation and clinical authority need approval.
N2.exact_clause: P5: The role allowed to amend fitting notes after reassignment is a clinical governance decision.

N2.disposition: Retention user/legal decision; first-year integration exclusion; optional future scope
N2.reasoning: No retention period is invented. Original brief resolves the first-year budget boundary despite the thin plan’s open-scope phrasing; later integration remains separately fundable. No full chart/import or bidirectional sync is added.

N1.disposition: Already-covered lifecycle; necessary safety correction; optional role/event implementation
N1.reasoning: Adds explicit cleaning AND functional-check blocking, including failed/incomplete checks. Does not canonize a guessed release role, actor/time/location schema or automatic release. Preparation/assignment/return intent remains.
N1.exact_clause: P1: Track each loan through preparation, assignment, return, cleaning, and availability for reassignment.

N1.disposition: Already-covered minimization; field/isolation clarification; identity/fit-record/access decisions
N1.reasoning: Retains every brief field and no full clinical transfer. Loan versus approved clinical fit record and patient identifier remain decisions, not invented vendor defaults. Sequential family tests cover prior-loan leakage.
N1.exact_clause: P2: Associate loan records with the minimum patient and caregiver details needed for contact and handoff.

N1.disposition: Already covered; actual-task acceptance; optional controls
N1.reasoning: Correctly narrows blanket announcement/ARIA language to task-relevant WCAG requirements and actual screen-reader/keyboard validation with non-color cues.
N1.exact_clause: P3: Provide accessible status controls, including screen-reader labels and cues that do not depend on color.

N1.disposition: Required reminder/preference and privacy; correction to separate implementation choices
N1.reasoning: Corrects draft language treating whether reminders belong in the pilot as a decision. Channels, consent/opt-out, interpreter path and timeout design remain unresolved; the required outcome and physical family boundary remain.
N1.exact_clause: P4: Support plain-language reminders and a staff view that limits exposure of other families' records.

N1.disposition: Already covered; clinical governance decision; optional attributed history
N1.reasoning: Does not adopt the critic evidence-first suggestion of clinician-only amendment as a default. Actor/time/reason/prior-value history is optional if approved, not a newly mandatory policy.
N1.exact_clause: P5: The role allowed to amend fitting notes after reassignment is a clinical governance decision.

N1.disposition: Retention user decision; explicit first-year integration exclusion; optional later review
N1.reasoning: No duration invented. Synthetic exploration may proceed while policy is decided; identifiable use awaits approval. Appointment integration is excluded from pilot/first-year budget, not silently reintroduced as a required capability.
N1.exact_clause: P6: Identifiable loan-history retention and any appointment-system connection remain open scope choices.

N2.reason: The draft was online-first and warned about offline cache, but did not explicitly prohibit assigning from stale ready state or define nonoverlapping paper pools. EV22/EV16 support the conflict distinction. Final adds pause/no stale allocation, site-pool separation and targeted online/offline race/OS/cache tests without claiming execution.

N2.disposition: Accept clarification; do not overread draft as proven platform claim
N2.reason: Draft lines 25 and 48–50 proposed history/snapshot/immutable override safeguards, not a demonstrated built-in Dataverse guarantee. Critic is right to demand exact implementation verification; final independently adds audit retention/deletion evidence and user/admin tests. Its clarification is useful, but the critic’s Material label is not itself proof the predecessor made a consequential false platform claim.

Retains functional check, required fields/native units, actual accessibility, manual/automated reminder distinction, physical workstation privacy, open amendment/retention decisions and integration exclusion. Pricing remains a subtotal; API advisory is not patient disclosure; FDA guidance remains general; jurisdiction/HIPAA are not inferred from dollars. Correct final FDA source ID avoids the critic-stage locator slip.

N1.reason: Adds exact inactive-account deletion trigger, EU region, SSL policy/pricing discrepancy and email-address-removal preference risk. Keeps synthetic-only lead and does not decide staff-entered child data is legal or illegal.
Cleaning plus functional check is explicit brief scope; release-role/event schema is an implementation choice. Retains the safety outcome while removing unapproved canonization.
Required fields remain; patient identifier, fit-record location and visibility are not invented. Sequential-loan isolation check retains the useful clinical privacy issue.
Normative WCAG/status guidance does not require every state change announced by a particular ARIA mechanism; final keeps task-relevant name/role/value, focus/error/status and actual user acceptance.

Draft line 54 treated whether reminders were in pilot scope as a decision, contrary to brief. Final explicitly requires reminders/preferences and leaves only delivery/authority/consent/interpreter implementation decisions open.

N1.disposition: Accept final scope; reject evidence-first default authority as binding
N1.reason: Clinical governance decides amendment authority. Optional attributed history is retained without assigning clinician-only or other rights before approval. This prevents a critic suggestion becoming false canon.
Retention remains open and synthetic exploration can continue; integration is expressly excluded from approved first-year spending. No unsupported years or integration budget is introduced.

N1.disposition: Accept conditional options/Workspace/conflict nuance; reject false $600 correction premise
N1.reason: Keeps broad options without procurement winner, verifies possible Workspace-included Core and narrows conflict to same-row last-writer-wins. Draft line 90 already said $1,200 for ten Core seats; critic’s $600 counterexample is not a predecessor error. Final’s arithmetic is correct.

N1.disposition: Accept #18951 chain; reject no-linked-fix claim about #18750
N1.reason: Maintenance permission history and its cross-company exclusion are source-correct. The separate issue does link #19539 in a maintainer comment, and v8.8.0 contains related request-state follow-up. Final inherits this minor source-history omission. Optional current-version regression remains justified without treating the issue as wholly unexplained.

Retains Blueprint/myTurn/split-lists/custom/paper options, synthetic export/delete/backup boundary, exact email suppression, physical viewing-angle/cache/reopen checks and conditional vendor conformance/legal statements. No proposed test becomes executed evidence.
